summary: rl.question() shows a prompt, waits for the user to type, and gives back the text. Use it to get a name, a number, or any answer.
notes: await pauses until the user presses Enter. await only works inside an async function, so the code is wrapped in main().
The answer is always a string. typeof rawAge shows string.
Number(rawAge) converts the text to a number. rl.close() lets the program end.
pitfall: Writing rawAge + 1 without Number() gives "161" with no error, because + joins two strings instead of adding.
contrast: Like Python's input(), rl.question() always gives back a string. Unlike Python and Java, reading input is asynchronous, so you write await inside an async function.
